record.paper_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
record.original_question: What is the continuum-limit behavior of the Roberge-Weiss endpoint and related critical temperatures for Wilson-fermion lattice QCD, and can the continuum extrapolation be achieved there? This asks whether the qualitative picture known from staggered-fermion studies survives quantitatively when Wilson fermions are pushed to the continuum limit.

evidence.quote: This is an open problem because the continuum extrapolation of Tc has not yet been achieved for the Wilson fermion.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider lattice QCD with Nf=2 mass-degenerate Wilson fermions at finite temperature in the presence of an imaginary quark chemical potential μ = iμ_I. The grand-canonical partition function is periodic in θ = μ_I/T with period 2π/3, and along the lines θ = (2k+1)π/3 there is a first-order Roberge–Weiss (RW) transition associated with the spontaneous breaking of charge-conjugation symmetry above a critical temperature T_RW. The RW endpoint at T = T_RW depends on the quark mass m: it is first-order (triple point) for sufficiently small or sufficiently large m, and second-order (Ising) for intermediate masses, with two tricritical mass values m_tric^(light) and m_tric^(heavy) separating these regimes.

(a) Determine the continuum-limit values of the RW endpoint temperature T_RW and of the tricritical quark masses m_tric^(light), m_tric^(heavy) for Nf=2 Wilson-fermion lattice QCD, by performing a controlled continuum extrapolation Nτ → ∞ (with aspect ratio fixed and Nτ a = 1/T).

(b) Determine the continuum-limit value of the pseudocritical/critical temperature T_c at zero chemical potential for Nf=2 Wilson fermions, and verify whether the qualitative phase-structure picture established with staggered fermions (location of the RW endpoint, mass dependence of its order, position of the tricritical points) is reproduced quantitatively by Wilson fermions in the continuum limit.
artifact.status_search_result: Lattice studies of the Roberge–Weiss endpoint with Nf=2 Wilson fermions have been carried out at Nτ=4 and Nτ=6, with exploratory Nτ=8 results. These studies report that the tricritical masses shift toward smaller values as the lattice is refined and explicitly state that significantly finer lattices are needed before a continuum extrapolation becomes feasible. No continuum-extrapolated result for T_RW or T_c with Wilson fermions at finite (imaginary) chemical potential is reported in the available literature, indicating the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Roberge-Weiss transition in Nf=2 QCD with Wilson fermions and Nτ=6
status_evidence.snippet: Compared to Nτ=4 lattices, the tricritical masses are shifted towards smaller values. Exploratory results on Nτ=8 as well as comparison with staggered simulations suggest that significantly finer lattices are needed before a continuum extrapolation becomes feasible.
status_evidence.claim: Continuum extrapolation of the RW endpoint with Wilson fermions has not yet been achieved; finer lattices required.

status_evidence.title: The nature of the Roberge-Weiss Transition in Nf=2 QCD with Wilson Fermions
status_evidence.snippet: Finite size scaling for Nf=2 Wilson fermions on Nτ=6, with comparison to staggered results, indicates substantial cut-off effects on the tricritical masses.
status_evidence.claim: Cut-off effects remain large for Wilson-fermion RW endpoint, continuum limit not reached.
